Grammar · Lesson 11

Past states with was and were

Use the past of be to locate and describe earlier situations: I was at home, They were tired, and Were you busy?

Was and were are not new grammar. They are the same verb be you learned first, moved onto yesterday’s timeline.

Discovery check: choose the past form

Read the subject first. I, he, she, and it take was; you, we, and they take were.

1I tired last night.
2We at the station at six.
3It cold yesterday, so we sat outside.
4They at the meeting, so I sent them the notes.
5The train full this morning, so I stood the whole way.
6Where you two hours ago?

The system: was and were

You already know this verb. In the present it is am, is, are. To move it to the past, am and is become was, and are becomes were. Nothing else in the sentence changes; only the time moves.

present (today)past (yesterday)
I am tired. / She is tired.I was tired. / She was tired.
You are tired. / They are tired.You were tired. / They were tired.
I / he / she / ityou / we / they
positiveI was at home.They were at home.
negativeShe wasn’t at home.We weren’t at home.
questionWas he at home?Were you at home?

Short answers: Yes, I was. / No, they weren’t. Do not repeat the place or adjective in a short answer.

Get to the root: move a state onto a past timeline

Was/were is the past form of be. It connects a person or thing to a description, identity, age, condition, or location at an earlier time. It does not normally describe an action; it tells us what the situation was.

past connectionexampleinformation
locationWe were in Oaxaca.where we were
conditionI was tired.how I felt
descriptionThe hotel was quiet.what it was like
identity / roleShe was my manager.who she was then
ageHe was twenty.his age then

Time expressions that point to the past

A past-time expression tells the listener where to place the situation. When you hear or use one of these, present am, is, are switches to was, were. Once the past time is clear from context, you do not need to repeat it in every sentence.

expressionexample
yesterdayThe office was quiet yesterday.
last night / last weekWe were at a concert last night.
two hours agoShe was here two hours ago.
in 2020I was in Lisbon in 2020.

A small past scene

The meeting was on Tuesday. It was at a hotel downtown. The room was small, but the chairs were comfortable. About twenty people were there.

After the first sentence establishes Tuesday, every following was/were naturally belongs to that same past scene.

Why was and were do the grammar work

Be is unusual: it makes its own negatives and questions and never needs the helper do / did. Was/were agrees with the subject, moves to the front for questions, and combines directly with not.

Follow the moving part

The meeting was long. → Was the meeting long? → The meeting wasn’t long.

Only was moves or becomes negative. This is why Did the meeting was long? mixes two different systems and is not the target form. Compare an action verb: Did she work? But with be: Was she at work?

There was / there were: the past of there is / there are

You can move there is / there are onto the same past timeline. Say There was a problem for one thing and There were two empty seats for plural things. Questions follow the same movement: Was there a problem? Were there any seats?

Born uses was / were

English says I was born in 1990 and They were born in Brazil. Treat was/were born as a useful fixed chunk. Ask Where were you born?, not Where did you born?

Drill 8: say it, then reveal

Read the cue, say the full sentence aloud, then reveal only after you answer.

1 I am busy. Change to yesterday.

I was busy yesterday.

2 There are two problems. Change to the past.

There were two problems.

3 The coffee was hot. Make it negative.

The coffee wasn’t hot.

4 They were at the bank. Ask the question.

Were they at the bank?

5 Was the movie good? Answer yes.

Yes, it was.

6 Were your friends at the game? Answer no.

No, they weren’t.

Use it in real life

Yesterday, three times: Say where you were yesterday at nine in the morning, at three in the afternoon, and at nine at night. At nine I was at my desk.
Last weekend: Describe your last weekend with was and were. Where were you? Who was with you? How was the weather?
Ask the teacher: Ask five questions that begin Where were you…? and listen for the short answers. Where were you last Friday at eight?
A place you visited: Think of a place from a past trip and describe how it was. The streets were crowded. The food was excellent.
Childhood: Say three true sentences that begin When I was a child… When I was a child, our apartment was small.
